_meta.description: GitLab Epic documentation templates — optimized for progressive disclosure, visual scannability, and decision-forward structure. Inspired by Google Design Docs, Amazon 6-Pagers, and Stripe engineering practices.

changelog.2.1.0: Removed TL;DR (merged into Objective), removed manual TOC (GitLab handles natively), renamed 'Metadata Header' to 'Epic Status'

Epic Status.hint: Use reviewer status emoji (✅ ⏳ 🔄) for instant review-state visibility

Objective.hint: What are we doing, why, and what's the expected business outcome? This is the first thing anyone reads — make it count.

Business Context & Problem Statement.hint: Lead with data. What pain exists today? Quantify the cost of inaction.

Business Objectives.hint: SMART format — Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: Non-scope is equally important as scope. List what this initiative deliberately excludes and why.

Stakeholders & RACI.hint: Each row must have exactly ONE Accountable person. Bold the R and A cells.

Requirements.hint: Each requirement gets 30–80 words max. Use priority emoji for visual scanning.

Success Metrics.hint: Every metric must be quantified. 'Improve performance' is not a metric.

Risk Assessment.hint: Show 5×5 heat map first using colored emoji (🟢🟡🟠🔴), then detailed register table below.

Next Steps & Decision Log.hint: Use GitLab task lists (- [ ]) for action items. Decision log captures key choices made.

Glossary.hint: Use GitLab description list syntax for clean term definitions

business_requirement.description: Business requirements focusing on ROI, stakeholder value, strategic alignment, and measurable outcomes. Uses RACI matrices, risk heat maps, and SMART objectives.

Epic Status.hint: Use Stripe-style gavel block — each reviewer gets status emoji showing approval state

Objective.hint: What are we building, why, and what's the key architectural decision? One paragraph that gives full context.

Context & Motivation.hint: What problem does this solve? What triggered this work? Include links to relevant issues/epics.

Goals & Non-Goals.hint: NON-GOALS are the most important part. List things that could reasonably be goals but are deliberately excluded.

Architecture Overview.hint: Include a mermaid architecture diagram. The diagram IS the source of truth — no stale images.

Data Model & Storage.hint: Schema definitions, storage choices, data lifecycle

API Contracts.hint: Request/response examples in JSON code blocks. Use inline diff ({+ new +} / {- old -}) for changes.

Key Algorithms & Logic.hint: Only for non-trivial logic. Skip if straightforward CRUD.

Alternatives Considered.hint: ⭐ THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION (per Google). Shows rigorous thinking. Each alternative gets 100–200 words.

Implementation Plan.hint: Break into shippable increments. Each phase should deliver testable value.

Open Questions.hint: Use GitLab task lists: - [ ] Question (@owner, due: date). Close as decisions are made.

Decision Log (ADRs).hint: MADR format: Status → Context → Decision Drivers → Considered Options → Decision Outcome

Definition of Done.hint: Use GitLab three-state task lists: [x] done, [ ] pending, [~] not applicable

Appendix.hint: Extended analysis, raw data, detailed calculations. Use <details> tags.

technical_design.description: Technical design documents following Google's design doc philosophy — context, goals/non-goals, proposed design, alternatives considered, and cross-cutting concerns. Emphasizes demonstrating rigorous thinking through explicit trade-off analysis.

Objective.hint: What user problem are we solving, and how will we know we've solved it? Lead with the user impact.

Problem Statement.hint: Lead with evidence — user research data, support ticket volume, funnel drop-off rates. Not assumptions.

User Stories.template:
**US-{nn}: {title}**
As a [persona], I want [action] so that [outcome]
**Acceptance Criteria:** [testable criterion]
User Stories.hint: Each user story MUST begin with a bold, scannable title in the format 'US-01: One-Click Reorder' followed by the As a… statement. Titles should be unique, concise (3-6 words), and action-oriented. Each story must map to at least one testable acceptance criterion listed directly below it.

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: Non-scope prevents scope creep. Be explicit about what's out for V1 and what's deferred to V2.

User Flows.hint: Include mermaid flowcharts for happy path AND key error paths. Don't just document the sunshine scenario.

Non-Functional Requirements.hint: Be specific: 'P99 latency < 200ms' not 'should be fast'

Launch Plan.hint: Feature flag strategy, rollout percentage plan, rollback criteria, A/B test design if applicable

UX/Design.hint: Link to Figma/mockups. Describe key interaction patterns and accessibility requirements.

Competitive Analysis.hint: How do competitors solve this problem? What can we learn?

feature_specification.description: Feature specifications that bridge product and engineering — evidence-based problem statements, user stories with acceptance criteria, explicit edge cases, launch plans with rollback criteria, and measurable success metrics.

Objective.hint: What does this API do, who consumes it, and what's the key design principle?

Overview & Authentication.hint: Base URLs per environment, auth mechanism (OAuth2/API key/JWT), token lifecycle, scopes/permissions

Resource Definitions.hint: One table per resource. Include validation rules and constraints.

Endpoints.hint: Working examples are mandatory. Use diff code blocks ({+ new +} / {- old -}) for versioned changes.

Error Handling.hint: Standardized error envelope. Include request_id for debugging. Group by category (auth, validation, server).

Pagination & Rate Limiting.hint: Exact numbers: requests/minute, burst limit, pagination cursor vs offset, max page size, rate limit headers

Webhooks & Events.hint: Include payload examples. Specify at-least-once vs at-most-once delivery. Document idempotency keys.
Webhooks & Events.conditional: Include only if API has event-driven components

Versioning & Deprecation.hint: URL vs header versioning, backward compatibility guarantees, deprecation timeline, sunset headers

Changelog.hint: Use inline diff syntax for schema changes. Flag breaking changes with > [!caution] alerts.

Testing & Sandbox.hint: Sandbox URLs, test credentials, mock data, Postman collection link

api_specification.description: API specifications modeled after Stripe's gold standard — working examples for every endpoint, standardized error envelopes, explicit rate limits, webhook delivery guarantees, and versioning strategy. Developer experience is the primary design constraint.

Objective.hint: What infrastructure are we building/changing, why, and what are the key SLA targets?

Business Context.hint: Why does the business need this infrastructure? What happens if we don't build it?

SLA/SLO Requirements.hint: Availability, latency percentiles, throughput, error rate. Current vs target.

Architecture Overview.hint: Mermaid architecture diagram is mandatory. Show all services, data stores, network boundaries, and traffic flow.

Component Design.hint: One subsection per major component: compute, storage, networking, CDN, queues, etc.

Environments & CI/CD.hint: Include pipeline diagram (mermaid) showing build → test → stage → prod flow

Disaster Recovery.hint: Include explicit RPO/RTO targets per failure scenario. When was the last DR drill?

Scaling Strategy.hint: Horizontal vs vertical. Auto-scaling policies. Include cost implications at scale.

Cost Analysis.hint: Include current spend vs projected spend. Flag top 3 cost drivers.

Operational Runbooks.hint: Index of runbooks with links. Detailed procedures live in separate docs.

Migration/Cutover Plan.hint: If this replaces existing infra, include cutover steps and rollback procedure

infrastructure_design.description: Infrastructure design documents emphasizing operational readiness — explicit SLA/SLO targets, cost analysis, disaster recovery with tested RPO/RTO, observability with alerting rules, and scaling strategies with cost implications. Every component must answer: how does it fail, how do we know, how do we recover?

Objective.hint: What are we migrating, from where to where, when, and what's the rollback window?

Current State.hint: Architecture diagram of current system. Include known pain points, technical debt, and failure modes.

Target State.hint: Architecture diagram of target system. Highlight what changes and what stays the same.

Migration Strategy.hint: Big-bang vs phased vs trickle. Lift-and-shift vs re-platform vs re-architect. Justify the choice.

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: What's included in this migration phase? What's explicitly deferred?

RACI Matrix.hint: Migration plans cross multiple teams. RACI eliminates 'I thought they were doing that' failures.

Risk Assessment.hint: ⭐ HIGHEST-STAKES DOCUMENT TYPE. Risk assessment must be thorough. Include contingency plans, not just mitigations.

Timeline & Milestones.hint: Include Gantt chart via mermaid. Each milestone needs explicit go/no-go criteria.

Cutover Plan.hint: Step-by-step numbered procedure. Include time estimates per step, responsible person, and verification checks.

Rollback Plan.hint: Explicit triggers (what conditions activate rollback). Step-by-step procedure. Maximum rollback window. Data reconciliation steps.

Dry Run Plan.hint: When, how many dry runs, success criteria

Data Security & Compliance.hint: Data classification, encryption in transit/at rest, access controls during migration, audit trail, compliance requirements

Communication Plan.hint: Who needs to know what, when? Include customer-facing comms if applicable.

Post-Migration Support Plan.hint: Hypercare period, escalation paths, known issues watchlist, performance monitoring period

Lessons Learned.hint: Fill in post-migration. Template exists so it doesn't get forgotten.

migration_plan.description: Migration plans as operational playbooks — current/target state architectures, explicit RACI ownership, risk heat maps with contingency plans, step-by-step cutover and rollback procedures, dry run plans, and communication matrices. Designed for the highest-stakes document type in engineering.

full_read: all sections including Cutover and Rollback procedures

Objective.hint: What systems are being integrated, what data flows between them, and what's the SLA?

Integration Overview.hint: System context diagram showing all participating systems, direction of data flow, and integration pattern (sync/async/event).

Data Contract & Mappings.hint: Include schema validation rules. Use inline diff for contract changes.

Error / Retry Path.hint: DO NOT SKIP. Error flows are where integrations actually fail.

Error Handling & Recovery.hint: Retry policies: max attempts, backoff strategy (exponential/linear), circuit breaker thresholds.

Monitoring & Alerting.hint: Monitor integration health, not just system health. Track: message throughput, error rate, latency, queue depth.

Versioning & Backward Compatibility.hint: How are breaking changes handled across system boundaries? Contract versioning strategy.

Fallback & Degradation.hint: What happens when the integration is down? Graceful degradation strategy, cached responses, circuit breakers.

Operational Runbook.hint: Troubleshooting guide: common failures, diagnostic steps, resolution procedures. Wrap in <details> tags.

integration_spec.description: Integration specifications as enforceable contracts — explicit data mappings, sequence diagrams for happy AND error paths, retry policies with circuit breaker thresholds, SLA definitions with breach escalation, and monitoring that tracks integration health specifically. Error flows are required, not optional.

full_read: all sections including sequence diagrams and error handling
